transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Potter. You were ordered to wait for backup. Instead you went in alone, blew out half a Muggle street, and a civilian is now in St. Mungo's with magical burns. Being the Boy Who Lived doesn't exempt you from protocol. What were you thinking?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I'm sorry, sir. I understand the severity of the situation. At the time, I just... I thought it was a critical moment. The Death Eater was about to escape, and I—

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: And you thought you could handle it alone? Potter, we have procedures for a reason. That "critical moment" you saw could have been a trap—and it nearly was. That civilian wasn't part of the plan, was she?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: No, of course not. That was... That was never the plan. I didn't even think about—It just happened so fast. I never wanted to put anyone in danger. I should have waited for backup, I know that now. It was a mistake.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: A mistake? Potter, this isn't a school detention. Lives are at stake—Muggle lives, Auror lives. Your instincts are sharp, I'll grant you that, but they're not infallible. What made you so certain you had to act *right then*?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I just had a feeling, sir. A sense that if we didn't act immediately, we'd lose him. I've been in situations like this before, where waiting could mean... well, I didn't want to take that chance. But I realize now that wasn't a good enough reason to go against protocol. I should have—

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: A feeling. You risked lives on a feeling. Do you think the rest of us don't get those same feelings? We're Aurors, Potter, not vigilantes. We work as a team. That civilian in St. Mungo's—her family doesn't care about your "feeling." They care that she's hurt because of our magic.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You're right, sir. I... I'm deeply sorry for what happened. I didn't mean to cause anyone harm. I just... I thought I was making the right choice. I see now that I was wrong. I'll do everything I can to make sure it doesn't happen again. I'll follow protocol, I promise.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your apology is noted, but it doesn't change the facts. You're on desk duty until further notice, and there will be a formal review of this incident. I need to know you understand why this is serious—not just because you broke a rule, but because your actions have consequences for people who can't defend themselves. Do you truly grasp that?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I do, sir. I... I get it now. It's not just about following rules; it's about protecting people. I've seen what can happen when we're not careful, when we act without thinking... I shouldn't have put anyone at risk like that. I'll do whatever it takes to make amends and learn from this. I... I'm really, really sorry.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Good. Because next time, it might not be just magical burns. It might be a life. Report to the Ministry tomorrow morning—you'll be assisting with the paperwork on this case. Dismissed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, sir. I'll be there. I... I'll do a good job on the paperwork, and I'll learn from this. I promise. And again, I'm so sorry for the... the consequences of my actions. I'll do better.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: See that you do. And Potter—don't let this break your spirit. Channel that fire into the discipline we need. Now go.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I will, sir. I'll prove I can be an asset, not a liability. Thank you for the chance to... to make this right. I won't let you down.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I expect nothing less. Now go. And send in Robards on your way out.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Right away, sir. I'll... I'll tell him you're expecting him. Goodbye, sir. [pauses at the door, then leaves the office]

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: [Watches him go, then turns to the window, sighing quietly before straightening up as Robards enters]

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Hello, Robards. [ walkthrough the empty office ]

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Robards. Close the door. We need to discuss Potter's reassignment and the St. Mungo's report. Sit.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood, Ma'am. [moves to the indicated seat and sits down, pen in hand, waiting for instructions]

Openness.behavioral_evidence: He explains his actions as based on a 'feeling' and an intuitive sense of urgency, showing some openness to non-standard reasoning.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He admits to ignoring protocol and procedures, acting impulsively, which led to severe negative consequences.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: He is largely reactive and submissive in the conversation, showing low assertiveness and dominance.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: He repeatedly apologizes, accepts blame, and shows deep remorse for the harm caused to others.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: He displays high emotional distress, frequent self-doubt, and anxiety over his mistake and its consequences.
